b: As in the onset of '비', this sound occurs at the beginning of a syllable. In onset position it is a voiceless bilabial plosive: the velum closes the nasal passage, the two lips close, and they then open, releasing the air inside the mouth. In coda position, as in '읍', it is pronounced without releasing that air outward.
p: As in the onset of '피', this is a voiceless plosive. The velum closes the nasal passage, the two lips close, and they then separate with a strong release of air. When the letter is used in coda position, the sound is the same as '읍'.
bb: As in '삐', this sound occurs only in onset position. With the velum closing the nasal passage and the laryngeal muscles tensed, the two lips close and then open, releasing the air inside the mouth. It is a voiceless plosive.
d: As in the onset of '디', this sound occurs at the beginning of a syllable. The velum closes the nasal passage, and the tongue tip is placed against the upper alveolar ridge, blocking the oral passage and then releasing. It is a plosive. In coda position, as in '읃', the final release is not made.
t: As in '티', this sound occurs only in onset position. The velum closes the nasal passage, and the tongue tip is placed against the alveolar ridge and then released with a strong burst of air. It is a voiceless plosive. When the letter is used in coda position, only the closure between the tongue tip and the alveolar ridge is held, as with 'ㄷ' in '읃'.
dd: As in '띠', this sound occurs only in onset position. With the velum closing the nasal passage and the laryngeal muscles tensed, the tongue tip is placed against the upper alveolar ridge to block the oral passage and is then released forcefully. It is a voiceless plosive.
g: As in the onset of '기', this sound occurs at the beginning of a syllable. The velum closes the nasal passage, and the tongue root is raised against the soft palate, blocking the outgoing breath and then releasing. It is voiceless. In coda position, as in '윽', the tongue root is not released. Between vowels, as with 'ㄱ' in '아기', it is voiced.
k: As in the onset of '키', this sound occurs at the beginning of a syllable. The velum closes the nasal passage, and the tongue root is raised against the soft palate to block the oral passage and is then released with a strong burst of air. It is a voiceless plosive. In coda position it is the same as 'ㄱ' in '윽'.
gg: As in '끼', this sound occurs only in onset position. With the velum closing the nasal passage and the laryngeal muscles tensed, the back of the tongue body blocks the soft palate and then releases the outgoing breath. It is a velar plosive. In coda position it is pronounced as the same coda sound as 'ㄱ' in '윽'.
s: As in the onset of '시', this sound occurs at the beginning of a syllable. The tongue tip is raised almost into contact with the upper alveolar ridge, and the outgoing breath squeezes through that narrow gap, producing friction. It is voiceless. When the letter is used in coda position, as in '옷', the tongue tip closes against the alveolar ridge and the sound becomes the same as 'ㄷ' in '읃'.
ss: As in '씨', this sound occurs only in onset position. With the velum closing the nasal passage and the laryngeal muscles tensed, the tongue tip is raised almost into contact with the alveolar ridge or the hard palate, and the outgoing breath squeezes through that gap, producing friction. It is voiceless.
h: As in '히', this sound occurs only in onset position. It is a voiceless fricative made by narrowing the glottis while exhaling. When the letter is used in coda position, the tongue tip is held against the alveolar ridge without release, as with 'ㄷ' in '읃'.
j: As in '지', this sound occurs only in onset position. The front of the tongue body is placed broadly against the hard palate and then released, with friction produced at the same time. It is a voiceless affricate. In coda position the tongue tip closes against the gums and the sound becomes the same as 'ㄷ' in '읃'. Between vowels, as with 'ㅈ' in '모자', it is voiced.
ch: As in '치', this sound occurs only in onset position. The front of the tongue body is placed against the hard palate and, on release, a strong breath is expelled while friction is produced at the same time. It is a voiceless affricate. In coda position the tongue tip closes against the alveolar ridge and the sound becomes the same as 'ㄷ' in '읃'.
jj: As in '찌', this sound occurs only in onset position. With the velum closing the nasal passage and the laryngeal muscles tensed, the front of the tongue body is placed against the palate, blocking the outgoing breath, and friction is produced when it is released. It is a voiceless affricate.
n: As in the onset of '니', this sound occurs at the beginning of a syllable. The tongue tip is placed against the alveolar ridge and then released while the outgoing breath is sent out through the nostrils, so that the sound resonates in the nasal cavity. It is voiced. In coda position the tongue tip is not released.
m: As in the onset of '미', this sound occurs at the beginning of a syllable. The lips are closed, the outgoing breath is sent into the nasal cavity, and the vocal folds vibrate. It is voiced. In coda position the lips are not released.
ng: When it occurs as the onset of '이', it has no sound value. In coda position, as in '응', the tongue root is raised against the soft palate, the outgoing breath is blocked and then sent into the nasal cavity. It is a voiced nasal.
r: As in the onset of '리', this sound occurs at the beginning of a syllable. In onset position the tongue tip makes a single light tap against the upper alveolar ridge. In coda position, as in '을', the tongue tip is held firmly against the alveolar ridge and the air is released along both sides of the tongue, as a lateral.
